The source is a heavily deflected filament eruption observed well in GOES SUVI 304, from a small filament spanning approx. N16E12 to N25W00 (centered N25E05) at 2026-07-27T03:13Z when it began to slowly lift off, more fully lifting off past 2026-07-27T05:00Z, clearly deflecting sharply NE in the field-of-view. Field line movement and brightening in GOES SUVI 171 and dimming in GOES SUVI 195 was also observed.

The source is a filament eruption far-sided from Earth, observed first in GOES SUVI 304 as the filament eruption over the NW limb starting around 2026-07-27T05:13Z. STEREO A EUVI 195/304 also observes the eruption site after a data gap ends at 2026-07-27T07:05Z and 2026-07-27T07:15Z respectively, as dimming, double-ribbon flare, and post eruptive arcade centered approximately around N25W125.

Dimming is observed from the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery starting as early as 2026-07-29T21:00Z and an EUV wave is seen moving northeast of the eruption site from 2026-07-29T23:00Z to 2026-07-30T03:00Z, indicating northern deflection.

The source is associated with an M1.9 flare from AR 14492 peaking at 2026-07-30T17:00Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. This eruption is also observed as filament ejecta in SDO AIA 304 first lifting as early as 2026-07-30T15:18Z. SDO AIA 171/193 observe brightening, dimming, field line movement, EUV wave, and post-eruptive arcades.

data.note: Very faint feature first seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-31T03:24Z. This feature may be seen to the NNE in STEREO A COR2, but the image quality is too poor to be sure. The majority of the CME is obscured by the pylon in both SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME may be a filament eruption near the NW limb centered around N40-50W70-80 and best seen in SDO AIA 304 and SDO AIA 193. The filament starts to rise off the disk about 2026-07-31T00:30Z and "snaps" around 2026-07-31T02:00Z, but the majority of the associated material appears to fall back to the disk. Additionally, this CME may simply be outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z.

This is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z. No additional source has been identified for this front.

The source may be the cluster of AR 14498/14450, closer to AR 14498 as brightening near N15E29 surrounded by some weak dimming and field line movement in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-31T19:25Z.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 until a data gap begins at 2026-07-31T23:24Z. Also visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap ends at 2026-07-31T23:38Z. The source for this CME may not be clearly observed, with the only source candidate being on/near the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI, as field line movement around 2026-07-31T17:25Z in EUVI 195 and prominence brightening in EUVI 304 around 2026-07-31T18:45Z as a data gap begins. This source would be around approximately longitude W156.2 with STEREO A at W66.2, and triangulation supports approximately E166, so would be far to be the source match. This CME front was originally analyzed to an on-disk source, updated to be far-sided with more coronagraph imagery available afterwards to triangulate.

The source is most likely a small piece of ejecta seen over the NE limb in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2026-08-02T09:09Z.

data.note: CME observed best to the E in STEREO A COR2. Also observed faintly to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 until a downlink gap begins at 2026-08-03T05:00Z, and faintly to the W in GOES CCOR-1. The source may be gradual field line brightening/opening from AR 14501 (S07W43) lasting from approximately 2026-08-03T00:00Z to 2026-08-03T04:00Z in SDO AIA 193/211. The CME is likely deflected northeastward with proximity to the large southern polar coronal hole seen facing STEREO A EUVI.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in only STEREO A COR2, likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The CME is unavailable in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 real-time due to a downlink gap. The likely source is AR 14498, observed in SDO AIA 304 first as a filament liftoff with surface brightening starting around 2026-08-03T07:10Z, followed by a wider swath of faint dimming and brightening starting around 2026-08-03T08:16Z in SDO AIA 171/193, all centered ~N22W12.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D analysis using N22W12 as the approximate source, finding some northward deflection. May be some variance in the parameters without other coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: CME observed to the SE in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is a filament eruption on the south central disk centered around S35W05. The filament in SDO AIA 304 begins to lift as early as approximately 2026-08-03T03:00Z, with most of the eruption seen from 2026-08-03T07:00Z to 2026-08-03T12:00Z, with brightening on-disk. This CME is also observed in SDO AIA 193 as a wide swath of dimming starting at approximately 2026-08-03T10:00Z which migrates southeastward for several hours and covers a large area of the south-central disk. The filament eruption, field line movement, dimming, and brightening are also seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 at 2026-08-03T07:55Z and 2026-08-03T08:15Z respectively.

The source of this CME is a filament eruption seen from just beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304beginning at 2026-08-04T22:55Z along with field line opening visible in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary plane-of-sky using a longitude of E90 and limited early frames of SOHO LASCO C2 imagery.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-05T01:26Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely a secondary filament eruption following the filament eruption that caused CME: 2026-08-04T23:48Z. This second filament eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 304 over the NE limb beginning around 2026-08-05T00:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-08-05T08:15Z. In real time, this CME is covered by data gaps between downlinks for SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, which later backfilled. The source of this CME is likely an eruption centered around N10E40-50 beginning as early as 2026-08-05T05:30Z. Some filamentary ejecta can been seen in SDO AIA 304 as well as a minor EUV wave followed by an area of dimming in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement based on additional available SOHO LASCO C3 imagery.
Very speculative, preliminary single coronagraph measurement based on source location.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 imagery and the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is visible in SOHO LASCO C3 at 2026-08-05T18:42Z after a downlink data gap but is out of the field of view in SOHO LASCO C2 in real-time. The source may be an eruption with moving field lines beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting at 2026-08-05T11:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the N in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-08-06T00:53Z. It is also partially seen to the NNE in GOES CCOR-1 around the pylon but is covered by a real time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source may be related to some minor field line movement seen beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-08-06T00:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the ENE in GOES CCOR-1 beginning as early as 2026-08-06T03:00Z. The start time is somewhat subjective because the early rise off the solar disk is very slow. This feature is only seen in GOES CCOR-1. The source may be related to some faint field line movement near the E limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning as early as 2026-08-05T23:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative plane-of-sky measurement based only on later frames of GOES CCOR-1. The early propagation of the CME is obscured by Earth-shine.

data.note: Very faint, narrow CME first seen to the NE is GOES CCOR-1. The feature is only seen in GOES CCOR-1 in real time. The source may be related to a very small piece of ejecta seen on the E limb in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-08-06T08:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single coronagraph view and on-limb source.

data.note: This CME is visible to the W/SW in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source of this CME is a filament eruption visible to the SW in STEREO A EUVI 304 around 2026-08-06T16:15Z with associated moving/opening field lines, dimming, and brightening visible to the SW in STEREO A EUVI 195. The source is in close proximity to an equatorial coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is no SOHO imagery available currently due to an on going data gap. There was likely deflection within the field of view due to proximity of a coronal hole.

data.note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-07T06:36Z. It is also seen to the E in GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. Only the earliest frames of SOHO LASCO C2 are seen in real time. Most of the propagation of the CME is covered by a real-time data gap between downlink periods in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is most likely an eruption just beyond the E limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 as opening field lines beginning around 2026-08-07T05:37Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

Fit of SH with CCOR-1 and COR2A. The SH measurement has higher uncertainty because it fits a wide range of lat/lon parameters. This measurement is the closest to lat/lon of the original LE measurement.

data.note: Very faint outflow-like CME to the NW after a few bad frames in SOHO LASCO C2. There is no clear source for this feature.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky parameters based on best fit of features in SOHO LASCO C2.

data.note: Narrow and semi-bright outflow like CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR-1. There is a data gap for this event in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be moving/opening field lines visible beyond the NE limb in SDO/AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-08-07T21:00Z, however it is not the best timing for the visible features in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 frames. The feature appears to deflect further north as it travels through the field of view which may have impacted the fit and initial measurement of this CME.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and faintly to the N in STEREO A COR2. This is the second in a quick series of fronts to the NE at 2026-08-07T21:00Z, 2026-08-08T23:00Z, and 2026-08-08T00:36Z. The source is lengthy continuous field line movement over the E limb in SDO AIA 171 as early as 2026-08-07T20:12Z, and the pulse of field line movement likely responsible for this front can be seen starting around 2026-08-07T21:03Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. This front is quite faint in COR2, but more visibly northward than the brighter, NE CME: 2026-08-08T00:36Z.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. This is the third in a quick series of fronts to the NE at 2026-08-07T21:00Z, 2026-08-08T23:00Z, and 2026-08-08T00:36Z. The source is lengthy continuous field line movement over the E limb in SDO AIA 171 as early as 2026-08-07T20:12Z, and the pulse of field line movement likely responsible for this front can be seen starting around 2026-08-07T23:03Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting the fit appears deflected westward to ~E74 from the observed SDO source likely on/just beyond the E limb.

data.note: CME observed to the N/NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and not yet in LASCO C3 before a DSN gap begins at 2026-08-08T05:00Z, to the N/NW in GOES CCOR-1 but heavily obscured by the pylon, and best to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source is a filament erupton in the north central disk; the full eruption spanning approximately N28E35 to N08W00, centered ~N20E10. Observed as the filament ejecta and double ribbon flare in SDO AIA 304 first lifting around 2026-08-08T00:48Z and fully erupting at 2026-08-08T02:10Z, and as a prominence on the NE limb of STEREO A EUVI 195/304. Also observed in SDO AIA 171/193/304 as dimming and field line movement, and a brief post eruptive arcade.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and 4 available frames of SOHO LASCO C2 due to the DSN data gap, and the GOES CCOR-1 pylon too heavily obscuring the leading edge to reliably track with.

data.note: Filament eruption observed to the SW in GOES CCOR-1 and as a SE halo in STEREO A COR2. Not observed yet in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to DSN gap starting 2026-08-08T05:00Z. The source is a long span filament eruption from the SW disk, with sharp eastward deflection observed better from STEREO A's perspective. The eruption starts around 2026-08-08T05:37Z, observed in SDO AIA 171/193/211/304 and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 as filament ejecta, double ribbon flare and brightening, field line movement, minimal dimming, and a post-eruptive arcade. The eruption spans approximately ~S20W40 to ~S15W90 (centered S17W65).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1, noting the eastward deflection from the observed source longitude as seen in STEREO A EUVI 304. This analysis captures the bulk of the bright LE material in both spacecraft.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-08-08T16:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small amount of field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-08-08T15:00Z located at approx. S15W55.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint, wide, slow CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the SW in STEREO A COR2. The source is clearly far-sided via CME triangulation, and may only be observed in GOES SUVI 284 as slow moving field lines over the SE limb starting as early as 2026-08-08T15:00Z the previous day; noting this observation as more speculative.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely on or very near the NE limb, observed as a filament eruption and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193/304 starting around 2026-08-09T02:52Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Manually selected start time at 2026-07-27T02:37Z via GOES-Pri X-ray flux timeline and SDO AIA 131. Manually calculated end time.
